grades.quote: the hardware page table refill or the software LDPTE instruction will automatically split the two page table entries in half according to the information of the huge page table entries and then fill in the TLB
grades.reason: LoongArch passage on how a huge-page entry is represented in the page table and handled during page walking. LDPTE or hardware refill splits it into two half-size entries for the TLB, with a 16KB standard page and 32MB huge page example. This covers representation of large mappings, but it does not cover how page size is selected.

grades.quote: which supports different page sizes for different table entries
grades.reason: LoongArch TLB organization: STLB uses one configured page size for all entries, and MTLB supports different page sizes per entry. This is relevant to page-size selection and multiple page sizes, but it does not describe how large page mappings are encoded in page tables.
Generic OS textbook exercises on virtual memory and page sizes. They give no information on how an architecture represents large pages or selects page size.

grades.quote: A large page size increases TLB reach and loosens the associativity constraints on virtually indexed, physically tagged caches.
grades.reason: RISC-V satp passage. It lists the MODE values that select the translation scheme (Sv32, Sv39, Sv48, Sv57), and its rationale text discusses page-size tradeoffs: large pages and TLB reach, internal fragmentation, a 4 KiB base page, and transparent superpages. It does not say how larger page mappings (superpage PTEs or leaf levels) are represented, and the MODE field selects the addressing scheme, not a page size. So it gives only limited auxiliary information.
